title: [SMF] Implement Recovery feature

labels.name: Help Wanted
labels.description: Maintainers are not working on this issue so community help is wanted.

labels.name: status:needs-planning
labels.description: Issue accepted and needs planning into milestones

body:
open5gs-smfd is currently missing this features. I may be working at this soon. (SGWC and any GTPv1C/GTPv2C in open5gs probably misses same features, but I only plan to work on SMF myself so far).

Here's an exhaustive list of what may be needed: (TTCN3 tests relate to osmocom's osmo-ttcn3-hacks.git GGSN_Tests and PGW_Tests testsuites).

[A] Have own persistent Recovery counter and announce it to peers:

- Read, increment and store it back to a file upon open5gs-smfd start. Configure destination file in open5gs-smfd.cfg. (TS 29.060 sec 11.4)
- GTPv1C: Transmit "Recovery" IE in CretePDPContextResponse, UpdatePDPContextResponse, EchoResp
- GTPv2C: Transmit "Recovery" IE in EchoReq+Resp, CreateSessionReq+Resp, CreateBearerResponse, BearerResourceFailureInd, ModifyBererReq+Resp, DeleteSessionResp, DeleteBearerResp (and some more)
- TTCN3: Update existing GGSN_Tests, PGW_Tests docker-playground test suites to configure the destination path

[B] Implement Handling of Recovery information from peers:

- GTPv1C: Parsing "Recovery" IE in CreatePDPContextReq, UpdatePDPContextReq, EchoResp. Already validated by TTCN3 test GGSN_Tests.TC_pdp_act2_recovery (currently failing).
- GTPv2C: Parsing "Recovery" IE in EchoReq+Resp, CreateSessionReq+Resp, CreateBearerResponse, BearerResourceFailureInd, ModifyBererReq+Resp, DeleteSessionResp, DeleteBearerResp (and some more)
- If recovery increase is detected, trigger internal tear down of connection (tear down PFCP, Gx, Gy).
    TTCN3: Write new test for PGW_Tests, adapt the one in GGSN_Tests to take into account PFCP, Gx, GY interface tear down.

[C] Implement active GTP Echo towards peers to discover if they are online

- Add config option to open5gs-smfd to configure the timeout. Leave it disabled by default.
- GTPv1C (example of implementation in https://osmocom.org/issues/4165).
- GTPv2C
- TTCN3: Since open5gs cannot be dynamically configured to start/stop echo requests like osmo-ggsn, we may need to adapt existing TTCN3 tests to allow receiving and answering those Echo Req at any time.
